match.reason: The bank point teaches self-determination as Indigenous decision-making power in Australia, not Wilson's Fourteen Points and post-WWI national self-determination of peoples in Europe and colonies, so it is a different idea at a different depth and context.

draft.title: The Fourteen Points and self-determination
card: In January 1918, United States President Woodrow Wilson set out Fourteen Points as a plan for peace. He wanted a fairer world after the war.
the idea that a people has the right to rule itself, rather than be ruled by an empire or foreign power.
Wilson's plan said borders in Europe should follow where peoples lived. This shaped new borders and new states, such as Poland and Czechoslovakia.
People in colonies heard the idea too, and many hoped it would apply to them. The peacemakers mostly did not extend it to colonies, so many were disappointed.
draft.remember: Self-determination means a people can rule itself. It shaped new borders and raised hopes in colonies.

opts: A people has the right to rule itself
A country has the right to take over its neighbours
A country must pay for the damage it caused
An empire may keep control of the lands it holds
a.why: Self-determination is the right of a people to govern itself. It is not about payment for damage, which is a different issue, or about empires keeping their lands.
a.clue: Think about who gets to make the rules for a people.

b.q: A newspaper in a colony in 1919 praises Wilson's plan. Why would many colonial readers have welcomed it?
opts: It suggested peoples might have the right to rule themselves
It promised that colonies would be given money by Europe
It ended the war and so removed all foreign rulers
It promised that every colony would join the United States
b.why: Wilson spoke of peoples ruling themselves, so colonial readers hoped it applied to them. It did not promise independence or money, and most colonies stayed under foreign rule.
b.clue: Which idea in the plan would appeal to people ruled by others?

a.best: A people has the right to rule itself

b.best: It suggested peoples might have the right to rule themselves

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedging qualifier ('might'). The others are absolute and implausible ('all foreign rulers', 'every colony would join the United States'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts check out. In question b, the right option is the only hedged one and the distractors are implausible, so it is easy to guess without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: The Fourteen Points and self-determination
card: In January 1918, United States President Woodrow Wilson set out Fourteen Points as a plan for peace. He wanted a fairer world after the war.
the idea that a people has the right to rule itself, rather than be ruled by an empire or foreign power.

proposal.remember: Self-determination means a people can rule itself. It shaped new borders and raised hopes in colonies.

opts: A people has the right to rule itself
A country has the right to take over its neighbours
A people must accept rule by the strongest power
An empire may keep control of the lands it holds
a.why: Self-determination is the right of a people to govern itself. It is the opposite of an empire or a strong power ruling over others, so the options about empires and strong powers are wrong.
a.clue: Think about who gets to make the rules for a people.

b.q: A newspaper in a colony in 1919 praises Wilson's plan. What in the plan would many colonial readers have welcomed?
opts: Its idea that peoples should rule themselves
Its promise of independence for all colonies
Its plan to make colonies pay war debts
Its call for empires to grow stronger
b.why: Wilson spoke of peoples ruling themselves, so colonial readers hoped the idea would apply to them. It was not a promise of independence for colonies: the peacemakers mostly did not extend it to them, which is why many were disappointed.
b.clue: Was it a promise to colonies, or an idea they hoped would reach them?

a.best: A people has the right to rule itself

b.best: Its idea that peoples should rule themselves
